title: Talazoparib · breast monotherapy
context_label: Germline BRCA1/2-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
schedule_summary: Talazoparib is taken once daily continuously until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The usual starting dose is 1 mg; kidney function, interactions and side effects can require a different prescription.
purpose: Control advanced cancer and symptoms while balancing side effects and treatment burden.
indication_text: Germline BRCA1/2-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
administration_text: Swallow capsules whole with water, with or without food. Do not open or dissolve them. If a dose is missed or vomited, take the next prescribed dose at its usual time; do not take a replacement or double dose.
monitoring_summary: Check FBC, kidney and liver function before starting and every four weeks. More frequent blood review may be needed for low counts; prolonged abnormalities require specialist assessment. Confirm the germline BRCA result and previous treatment. Review pregnancy status and contraception, kidney function and interacting medicines, particularly P-glycoprotein inhibitors.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Talazoparib
agents.mechanism: Disrupts DNA repair in BRCA-associated cancer
agents.explanation: Talazoparib inhibits PARP and traps it on damaged DNA. Cancer cells with inherited BRCA1/2 changes may have less ability to repair this damage. Normal bone marrow can also be affected, so blood-count monitoring is essential.
visual: BRCA-deficient cells less able to repair
agents.watch: Report fever, infections, unusual bruising, persistent fatigue or breathlessness.
risks: Anaemia, low white cells and platelets
Rare serious bone-marrow disorders including MDS/AML

sections.title: A daily routine
sections.text: Choose a consistent daily time. Check capsule strength after every dose change and arrange supplies before they run out.

sections.title: Reviews without routine infusion visits
sections.text: No port or infusion pump is needed for talazoparib itself. Blood tests, clinic review and scans still need appointments.

sections.title: A treatment hold
sections.text: Do not restart automatically when a calendar month has passed. The team reviews recovery and the next dose.

sections.title: After treatment
sections.text: Report persistent unexplained fatigue, infections or bruising; rare bone-marrow disorders can require investigation.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be chosen
evidence.intro: Talazoparib targets a DNA-repair vulnerability associated with inherited BRCA1/2 changes. Suitability also depends on HER2 status, previous anthracycline/taxane treatment and, for hormone-receptor-positive disease, previous endocrine treatment or its suitability.
evidence.population: Germline BRCA1/2-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer

support.title: Blood counts
support.text: Keep four-weekly blood reviews and any additional tests. Fever or unusual bleeding needs prompt advice.

support.title: Taking capsules
support.text: Use the strength and number on your current prescription. Do not replace a missed or vomited dose.

support.title: Nausea
support.text: Use the prescribed rescue plan; call if vomiting affects fluids or tablets.

support.title: Medicines review
support.text: Check every new medicine or supplement with the oncology pharmacist.

items.title: Your exact schedule
items.text: Talazoparib is taken once daily continuously until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The usual starting dose is 1 mg; kidney function, interactions and side effects can require a different prescription.

items.text: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.

chapters.title: Checks across treatment
chapters.intro: Your team arranges tests and reviews the results before treatment decisions.

items.title: Blood and organ checks
items.text: Check FBC, kidney and liver function before starting and every four weeks. More frequent blood review may be needed for low counts; prolonged abnormalities require specialist assessment.

items.title: Other treatment-specific checks
items.text: Confirm the germline BRCA result and previous treatment. Review pregnancy status and contraception, kidney function and interacting medicines, particularly P-glycoprotein inhibitors.

items.title: Cancer review and follow-up
items.text: Agree the scan type and review interval for the known disease sites. Review response, symptoms and toxicity together; new or worsening symptoms may need an earlier assessment.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Bone-health assessment follows endocrine therapy, ovarian suppression, menopause and other fracture risks. It has its own monitoring plan.

chapters.title: The wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Review response, toxicity and priorities to decide whether to continue, change or stop. Supportive and palliative care can accompany anticancer treatment.

items.title: Treatment changes
items.text: Do not replace a missed or vomited dose. Take the next dose at the usual time. The team decides whether and at what dose to restart after a hold.

items.title: Medicines review
items.text: Ask the pharmacist to review P-glycoprotein inhibitors and all new medicines or supplements. Changing kidney function or an interacting medicine can change the prescribed dose.

items.title: After treatment
items.text: Keep the agreed follow-up and report persistent or new symptoms between visits.
